extracted.intended_audience: Navy and Marine Corps commanders, public affairs officers (PAOs), and staff responsible for public/institutional communications and publications
extracted.subtask_description: Official Department of the Navy public affairs instruction covering policy and procedural standards for exhibits, music participation, environmental disclosures, entertainment-industry support, crisis communications, internal communications, and print information/products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit approval and non-endorsement policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibits generating national or corporate interest must be requested 90 days in advance via CHINFO or DIRPA and, if required, obtain ASD(PA) approval. Exhibits must not favor, or endorse in fact or appearance, a single commercial entity, group, profit or nonprofit corporation, sect, religious organization, fraternal or political organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for exhibits should be submitted 90 days before the desired date. See references and supplemental guidance for additional constraints and approval routing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interagency and overseas exhibits approval process
rubrics_metrics.description: Overseas and international exhibits of the U.S. Government will be approved by ASD(PA) via CHINFO and DIRPA and normally will not result in additional costs to DOD. Overseas commands shall forward requests via the combatant commander. For foreign trade shows or exhibitions, Defense Security Cooperation Agency is the approving authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All Navy activities forward requests to CHINFO; Marine Corps activities forward to DIRPA. Follow applicable Unified Command and host-nation arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of naval music participation (authorized activities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Military musical participation in public events is limited to patriotic programs rather than pure entertainment. Authorized participation includes music for presentation of national colors or military/patriotic music; music for public events and parades of general community interest open to the entire community; and incidental performances at admission-charging events where no additional charge is imposed to hear the band.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See supplemental guidance for authorized participation examples. Ensure the performance is incidental and open to the broader community; no extra fees for band attendance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on Navy musicians (unauthorized activities)
rubrics_metrics.description: DON musicians are not authorized to provide entertainment at luncheons, dinners, receptions, dances or other civilian-domain functions sponsored and attended primarily by persons not on active duty. Background, dinner, dance or social music is considered entertainment. Commercially sponsored events, events designed to increase business traffic, or events associated with particular religious, ideological or partisan political parties/movements will not receive band support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsor's charter or special relationship with Navy/Marine Corps is not sufficient for exception. Entertainment may only be provided at social functions sponsored by and intended for military personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music participation request and certification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Prospective civilian sponsors must submit requests for musical participation in COMREL events via DD Form 2536 and must certify there is no conflict with local civilian musicians; a statement from the cognizant local musicians' union must be attached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests should follow form requirements; failure to provide required certifications or union statement may result in denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music performance coordination and escalation
rubrics_metrics.description: Navy Bands coordinate with CHINFO (via the Music Program Liaison) and U.S. Marine Bands coordinate with DIRPA for approval of events where more than one military band is proposed; events of national/international importance; national sports/professional athletic events; national television or radio events; any travel outside the Continental U.S. (OCONUS) by US-based Navy bands; and events not otherwise meeting section conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain coordination/approval before committing to multi-band, national, televised, or OCONUS events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental public affairs release principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders and staffs shall: be prepared to grant public access to some draft and all final versions of unclassified documentation on environmental programs; offer prompt, full, and accurate disclosure in conformance with release principles and legal requirements; release information expeditiously and responsibly where public health concerns exist; be sensitive to affected civilian and military communities; and comply with federal, state, and local environmental laws and public involvement rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Chapter 2 release principles and referenced legal requirements. Be proactive and transparent, especially when public health is implicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entertainment-industry support approval authority
rubrics_metrics.description: ASD(PA) is the sole authority to approve DOD assistance to non-Government motion picture, television and video productions. After script and specific support requests (personnel, facilities, equipment) are reviewed and approved, ASD(PA) will set parameters for support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer all entertainment-industry inquiries to NAVINFO WEST, CHINFO, or ASD(PA); do not commit or promise support at the field level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field personnel prohibition on entertainment-industry commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Navy Public Affairs personnel in the field, their commanders or unit staff are not authorized to promise support or make commitments to entertainment industry representatives; all requests should be referred to NAVINFO WEST, CHINFO or ASD(PA) without commitments or hints of support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unauthorized promises may conflict with policy and create obligations; always use proper referral channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis communications principle: trust and credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective crisis communication depends on whether the command is perceived as trusted and credible; trusting relationships must be developed at the command level because improper handling can generate more publicity than the crisis and degrade mission accomplishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in pre-crisis relationship-building and consistent transparent communications to preserve credibility during crises.

rubrics_metrics.name: PAO role in crisis response
rubrics_metrics.description: PAO supports the command during crisis by managing information release and other public affairs aspects; PAOs or representatives must be available at all times, take immediate action, use mature judgment, and release appropriate information quickly and accurately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter 2 for release principles; prioritize timeliness, accuracy and chain-of-command coordination in crisis messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Affairs Guidance (PAG) requirement in crises
rubrics_metrics.description: The PAO shall generate Public Affairs Guidance (PAG) to support public discussion of the crisis. PAG should include an initial statement addressing basic facts as known and answer the most likely questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Chartroom online examples. PAG should be ready early and anticipate probable media/public questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual briefing of local officials and media
rubrics_metrics.description: At least once annually, major shore activities shall inform local news media representatives, civil defense, and law enforcement officials about standard plans to handle accidents and emergencies, and may use the opportunity to orient local media on DON and the command's function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overseas bases must conform to Unified Commander policies; exceptions exist for nuclear-related incidents covered elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control of video and photography on installations
rubrics_metrics.description: If no classified material is exposed, the commander may permit credentialed news photographers and electronic newsgathering teams to cover the event on U.S. military installations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow supplemental guidance for detailed procedures; always assess classification and security before granting access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on media authority off-base (domestic and foreign)
rubrics_metrics.description: Off-base in the U.S. or territories, naval officials' authority over news media is limited; the senior Navy/Marine official must determine whether classified information is present. Off-base in a foreign country, officials must conform to status-of-forces agreements, host-nation laws, and Unified Command instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult supplemental guidance for brief guidelines and coordinate with relevant authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confiscation procedures for photographic media
rubrics_metrics.description: If photographic media is confiscated as a last result, the command shall provide the photographer a receipt, must not detain the photographer, must review and remove classified portions then return edited media, and forward media believed to contain classified or sensitive information to the command Security Manager and notify CNO (N09N2) or CMC (Code INTC). All confiscations must be reported rapidly via the chain to CHINFO or DIRPA and the chain of command, preferably by telephone with message follow-up using OPREP 3 and Unit SITREP procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not detain media owners; ensure security review procedures are followed and timely notifications and reporting are made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal communications responsibilities for commanders
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders are responsible for the morale and esprit de corps of command members and shall implement a positive and effective internal communication plan with specified objectives, participate in long-term planning and day-to-day monitoring, and maintain routine liaison with the PAO to ensure the plan conforms to evolving command requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise leadership and attention to welfare; use internal communications to support morale and mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Affairs Officer responsibilities for internal communications
rubrics_metrics.description: PAOs shall implement an internal communication plan tailored to the command’s mission, clearly articulate mission/vision/goals, employ strategic thinking and sound writing, produce a variety of communication products appropriate to the command, provide measurable results, and keep CHINFO or DIRPA informed of significant local occurrences and lessons learned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAOs are responsible for the details and execution of internal communications; metrics and lessons learned should be reported upward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naval Media Center (NMC) role
rubrics_metrics.description: Under CHINFO supervision, the NMC generates internal communication products that support CHINFO policy and plans/executes functions to ensure broad vertical and horizontal communication using print, audio-visual, and electronic media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NMC supports CHINFO mission to keep Navy/Marine Corps personnel updated on issues affecting careers and lives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and message alignment for internal publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal publications are the commander's primary means to communicate mission-essential information to members; they should improve morale, increase knowledge, and ensure communication points align with DOD, DON, and other applicable guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure content supports command internal information objectives and is consistent with higher-level guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding restrictions for command newspapers
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of appropriated funds is authorized to establish a funded newspaper if a Civilian Enterprise (CE) newspaper is not feasible; the use of non-appropriated funds for any aspect of a newspaper operation is not authorized; appropriated funds shall not be used to pay any part of a commercial publisher’s cost in producing a CE publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CHINFO approval required to establish a funded publication; follow Navy Comptroller and DOD financial guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civilian Enterprise (CE) newspaper characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: CE newspapers are published under written contract between a commercial publisher and a command/installation; editorial content is the responsibility of the command PAO; publisher prints/distributes and incurs related expenses and offsets costs by selling advertising; commands are prohibited from using appropriated or non-appropriated funds to pay publisher costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CE contracts should delegate publication/distribution burdens to save taxpayer money while ensuring command communication needs are paramount; CE publications become property of the command upon delivery per contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funded newspaper characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Funded newspapers are fully funded by the public affairs allocation of a unit's operating fund, free from commercial advertising, and editorial content/layout is the responsibility of the command public affairs staff; printing is contracted commercially; installations with at least 500 members are eligible to produce an appropriated fund newspaper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CHINFO approval required prior to establishing a funded publication; non-appropriated funds may not be used for printing costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization conditions to establish/maintain unit newspapers
rubrics_metrics.description: Officers may establish unit newspapers provided: design, editorial development and distribution organized principally to improve morale/welfare; efficient use of funds/supplies/personnel; incorporate security and policy review into SOPs ensuring accurate review without undue delays; ensure newspaper supports DON and local PA objectives; sanctioned by local commander; obtain permission to publish from CHINFO (OI-4); establish only one newspaper per collocated location (host commander responsible).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow supplemental guidance for publishing conditions; CHINFO permission may not be delegated; Marine Corps commands follow MCO P5720.61.

rubrics_metrics.name: CE contract negotiation goals and scope delegation
rubrics_metrics.description: In negotiating CE contracts, commands shall seek to delegate as many publication and distribution functions as possible to the publisher to generate maximum savings, while ensuring command communication needs/requirements are paramount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracts should reflect appropriate guidance from references, cover local requirements, and aim to transfer burdens to the private sector while protecting editorial control and mission needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: CE publisher selection process and criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection group (senior command member as chair, staff/command judge advocate, procurement officer, printing representative, PAO as exec sec/editorial advisor, and other specialists) will hear presentations, review written data, inspect sites, investigate competence/reliability/technical/production/business capabilities, and consider that exchange of rights is a contractual consideration; only reputable firms shall be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only one bidder responds, the group may decline and pursue funded newspaper or negotiate via RFP; fair and equal opportunity afforded to responsible bidders; invite widest possible pool.

rubrics_metrics.name: CE contract terms: payments, duration, termination, editorial control
rubrics_metrics.description: A CE commercial publisher shall not pay money to the command; revenue sharing with a government agency is not authorized. CE contracts may be entered for one year with annual renewal options up to four years (then re-compete). Contracts must include termination for cause provisions. The contract must specify that the PAO or designated individual shall specify design/layout and editorial content while the publisher provides production and distribution services. Comic/feature supplements intended for distribution must have prior approval of the base commander.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document unsatisfactory performance for termination; selection group performs regular reviews to inform renewals/terminations; clauses should explicitly protect PAO editorial authority and command approval for supplements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising rules for CE publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts shall specify ground rules for advertising: publisher may place ads but shall not enter exclusive advertising agreements; commanders may require the publisher to enable free listings of personal items/services for members; advertisements for exchanges/commissaries/non-appropriated fund activities placed through the publisher; amount of advertising content will not exceed 60 percent of total newspaper (editorial-favoring ratios permitted if included in contract); commander may prohibit distribution on command property if advertising promotes dissident/protest activity or poses danger to loyalty/discipline/morale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before printing, review ads for illegality or threats to morale; request deletion in writing if offensive; if publisher refuses, commander may prohibit distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriated fund newspaper advertising policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Funded (appropriated fund) newspapers shall carry no commercial advertising; they may carry noncommercial news/announcements concerning non-appropriated fund activities and free listings of personal items/services representing incidental exchange among DON members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commanders may contract printing after CHINFO approval and must ensure adherence to NAVSO/NAVY Comptroller guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newspaper procedures: review, tenant support, localization, and reader feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Immediate superiors shall review subordinate newspapers to ensure compliance; host command newspapers will support tenant commands and provide balanced coverage; local news and information should be central and where feasible localize service-wide news by explaining local impacts; all newspapers must incorporate at least one means for reader feedback (letters to editor, guest columns, person-on-the-street interviews).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial policies and procedures support internal information objectives; ensure mechanisms for feedback and balanced coverage across local commands.
